canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_1 = (W_K, W_KP) ∈ O_P, where W_K is a weak compacton predicate for the K(m,n) equation and W_KP is a weak line compacton predicate for the KP(m,n) equation
canonical_goal.target_object: A rigorous weak-solution definition for compactly supported traveling waves of the one-dimensional equation u_t + a(u^m)_x + b(u^n)_{xxx} = 0 and compactly supported line traveling waves of the two-dimensional equation (u_t + a(u^m)_x + b(u^n)_{xxx})_x + σu_{yy} = 0, where m,n>0, m≠1, a,b∈ℝ\{0}, and σ∈{-1,1}.
feasibility_constraints: For the one-dimensional K(m,n) equation, the traveling-wave coordinate is ξ=x-ct, the profile parameter is g=c, the compacton profile satisfies U∈C^0_c(ℝ)∩L^max(m,n)_loc(ℝ), and every profile test function φ:ℝ→ℝ is smooth with compact support.

For the two-dimensional KP(m,n) equation, the line-wave coordinate is ξ=x+μy-νt, the profile parameter is g=ν-σμ^2, the compacton profile satisfies U∈C^0_c(ℝ)∩L^max(m,n)_loc(ℝ), and every profile test function φ:ℝ→ℝ is smooth with compact support.
The K(m,n) weak compacton predicate W_K(U) is ∫_ℝ((-gU+aU^m)φ' + bU^nφ''')dξ = 0 for every smooth compactly supported φ.
The KP(m,n) weak line compacton predicate W_KP(U) is ∫_ℝ((-gU+aU^m)φ'' + bU^nφ'''')dξ = 0 for every smooth compactly supported φ.

success_set.definition: Σ_1 = { (W_K,W_KP) : for every U∈C^0_c(ℝ)∩L^max(m,n)_loc(ℝ), W_K(U) holds exactly when u(t,x)=U(x-ct) satisfies ∬_ℝ×ℝ(uψ_t+au^mψ_x+bu^nψ_xxx)dt dx=0 for every smooth compactly supported ψ(t,x), and W_KP(U) holds exactly when u(t,x,y)=U(x+μy-νt) satisfies ∭_ℝ×ℝ^2(uψ_tx+σuψ_yy+au^mψ_xx+bu^nψ_xxxx)dt dxdy=0 for every smooth compactly supported ψ(t,x,y) }

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_2 = (C_K, C_KP, S_K, S_KP) ∈ O_P, where C_K and C_KP are weak cutoff feasibility predicates and S_K and S_KP are strong cutoff feasibility predicates
canonical_goal.target_object: A necessary-and-sufficient endpoint-exponent criterion for when a cutoff traveling-wave profile U_c(ξ)=U(ξ)H(L-|ξ|), with H(s)=1 for s>0 and H(s)=0 for s<0, is a weak compacton of the K(m,n) equation or a weak line compacton of the KP(m,n) equation, together with the corresponding endpoint-exponent criterion for when the same cutoff profile is a classical strong compacton solution.
feasibility_constraints: The support interval is [-L,L] with L>0, and the endpoint behavior is U(ξ)∼U_0(L-|ξ|)^p as ξ approaches ±L, where U_0∈ℝ\{0} and p∈ℝ\{0}.
For K(m,n), m,n>0, m≠1, a,b∈ℝ\{0}, g=c, U is C^3 on [-L,L], and U satisfies (-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'')'=0 for -L<ξ<L.
For KP(m,n), m,n>0, m≠1, a,b∈ℝ\{0}, σ∈{-1,1}, g=ν-σμ^2, U is C^4 on [-L,L], and U satisfies (-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'')''=0 for -L<ξ<L.

Define A_1=bU^n, A_2=b(U^n)', A_3=-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'', and A_4=(-gU+aU^m)'+b(U^n)'''. The K(m,n) weak cutoff predicate is A_1(±L)=A_2(±L)=A_3(±L)=0. The KP(m,n) weak cutoff predicate is A_1(±L)=A_2(±L)=A_3(±L)=A_4(±L)=0.

success_set.definition: Σ_2 = { (C_K,C_KP,S_K,S_KP) : C_K holds if and only if p>2/n; C_KP holds if and only if at least one of the following six alternatives holds: (1) p>max(1/m,3/n) and g=0; (2) p>max(1/m,3/n), m<1, and g≠0; (3) p>max(1,3/n), m>1, and g≠0; (4) 1≥p=2/(n-1), 2m+1>n≥3, g≠0, and U_0=(g(n-1)^2/(2bn(n+1)))^((n-1)/((n-2)(n+1))); (5) p=2/(n-m), n≥3m, g=0, and U_0=(-a(n-m)^2/(2bn(n+m)))^(1/(n-m)); (6) p=2/(n-m), m+2>n≥3m, g≠0, and U_0=(-a(n-m)^2/(2bn(n+m)))^(1/(n-m)); S_K holds if and only if p>3; and S_KP holds if and only if p>4 }

preference_ordering.definition: For two endpoint criteria q_1 and q_2 over the same equation family, q_1 ⪰_P q_2 if every endpoint exponent p admitted by q_2 is admitted by q_1. The weak criterion is strictly less restrictive than the strong criterion when there exists p such that C_K holds and S_K fails, or C_KP holds and S_KP fails.

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_3 = (F_exp,F_num) ∈ O_P, where F_exp is a finite catalogue of explicit cutoff compacton profile families and F_num is a family of numerically generated cutoff compacton profiles
canonical_goal.target_object: A nonempty catalogue of compactly supported weak compacton profiles U_c(ξ)=U(ξ)H(L-|ξ|) for the K(m,n) and KP(m,n) equations, including algebraic, cosine, Jacobi-cn, Jacobi-sn, rational Jacobi-cn, antisymmetric, and numerical profiles, such that each catalogue entry satisfies the relevant traveling-wave ordinary differential equation on -L<ξ<L and the relevant weak endpoint conditions at ξ=±L.
feasibility_constraints: Every explicit profile in F_exp has the cutoff form U_c(ξ)=U(ξ)H(L-|ξ|), where H(s)=1 for s>0 and H(s)=0 for s<0, L>0, and U(ξ)∼U_0(L-|ξ|)^p as ξ approaches ±L.
The allowed explicit profile templates are α(1-βξ^2)^p, αcos(βξ)^p, αsin(βξ)^p, αcn(βξ,k)^p, αcn(β(ξ+L/2),k)^p, αsn(βξ,k)^p, αsn(β(ξ+L),k)^p, and α((cn(βξ,k)+κ)/(cn(βξ,k)+γ))^q with κ,γ∈ℝ\{0}.

For every explicit profile template, the parameters α,β,k,κ,γ,q,L,g,m,n,a,b are feasible only when substituting U into (-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'')'=0 makes the coefficient of every linearly independent ξ-dependent expression equal to zero.
For a K(m,n) explicit weak compacton, the endpoint exponent and parameters must satisfy A_1(±L)=A_2(±L)=A_3(±L)=0, where A_1=bU^n, A_2=b(U^n)', and A_3=-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)''.
For a KP(m,n) explicit weak line compacton, the endpoint exponent and parameters must satisfy A_1(±L)=A_2(±L)=A_3(±L)=A_4(±L)=0, where A_4=(-gU+aU^m)'+b(U^n)'''.

A numerical profile in F_num is feasible only when V(ξ)=U(ξ)^n solves V''=2(C+(1+1/n)BV^(1/n)-(1+m/n)AV^(m/n)) on [-L,L], with A=2na/((m+n)b), B=2ng/((n+1)b), and the endpoint conditions V(±L)=V'(±L)=V''(±L)=0 for the K(m,n) weak compacton case or the corresponding A_1,A_2,A_3,A_4 boundary-vanishing conditions for the KP(m,n) weak line compacton case.

success_set.definition: Σ_3 = { (F_exp,F_num) : F_exp contains feasible weak compacton entries from the algebraic template α(1-βξ^2)^p, cosine template αcos(βξ)^p, Jacobi-cn templates αcn(βξ,k)^p and αcn(β(ξ+L/2),k)^p, Jacobi-sn templates αsn(βξ,k)^p and αsn(β(ξ+L),k)^p, rational Jacobi-cn template α((cn(βξ,k)+κ)/(cn(βξ,k)+γ))^q, and antisymmetric sine/Jacobi variants when p is an odd integer or odd rational power; F_exp includes weak-only cases in which the weak endpoint predicate holds and the strong predicate p>3 for K(m,n) or p>4 for KP(m,n) fails; F_num contains at least one profile generated by the V-equation whose transformed cutoff U_c=V^(1/n)H(L-|ξ|) satisfies the same weak integral identity as the corresponding K(m,n) or KP(m,n) compacton }

preference_ordering.definition: For two compacton catalogues F_1 and F_2, F_1 ⪰_P F_2 if every profile-template type represented in F_2 is represented in F_1 and every weak-only profile-template type represented in F_2 is represented in F_1. A weak-only profile-template type is a template for which the weak endpoint predicate holds for at least one admissible parameter choice and the corresponding strong endpoint predicate fails for that same parameter choice.

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_4 = T_K_to_KP ∈ O_P, where T_K_to_KP is a transfer predicate from one-dimensional K(m,n) compacton profiles to two-dimensional KP(m,n) line compacton profiles
canonical_goal.target_object: A conditional transfer theorem stating that a compactly supported scalar profile U satisfying the one-dimensional K(m,n) traveling-wave profile equation with parameter g also satisfies the two-dimensional KP(m,n) line-wave profile equation after choosing line-wave parameters μ and ν so that ν-σμ^2=g; for cutoff weak solutions, the transfer is valid only when the KP endpoint condition A_4(±L)=0 also holds in addition to A_1(±L)=A_2(±L)=A_3(±L)=0.
feasibility_constraints: The source profile U is compactly supported on [-L,L] and satisfies (-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'')'=0 for -L<ξ<L, with m,n>0, m≠1, and a,b∈ℝ\{0}.
The KP line-wave coordinate is ξ=x+μy-νt, with μ,ν∈ℝ and σ∈{-1,1}.
The KP line-wave parameter is matched to the K(m,n) profile parameter by ν-σμ^2=g.
For weak cutoff transfer, U_c(ξ)=U(ξ)H(L-|ξ|) must satisfy A_1(±L)=A_2(±L)=A_3(±L)=A_4(±L)=0, where A_1=bU^n, A_2=b(U^n)', A_3=-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'', and A_4=(-gU+aU^m)'+b(U^n)'''.

success_set.definition: Σ_4 = { T_K_to_KP : for every compactly supported U satisfying (-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'')'=0 for -L<ξ<L and for every μ∈ℝ and σ∈{-1,1}, setting ν=g+σμ^2 makes U satisfy (-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'')''=0 for -L<ξ<L as a KP(m,n) line-wave profile; if U_c=UH(L-|ξ|) also satisfies A_1(±L)=A_2(±L)=A_3(±L)=A_4(±L)=0, then u(t,x,y)=U_c(x+μy-νt) satisfies ∫_ℝ((-gU_c+aU_c^m)φ''+bU_c^nφ'''')dξ=0 for every smooth compactly supported φ }

robustness_scope.ambient_space: Δ_4 = { (U,m,n,a,b,g,μ,ν,σ,L) : U is compactly supported on [-L,L], m,n>0, m≠1, a,b∈ℝ\{0}, μ,ν,g∈ℝ, σ∈{-1,1}, L>0, and ν-σμ^2=g }

claimed_subfamily.definition: D_4 = { (U,m,n,a,b,g,μ,ν,σ,L)∈Δ_4 : U satisfies (-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'')'=0 for -L<ξ<L, and, for weak cutoff transfer, U_c=UH(L-|ξ|) satisfies A_1(±L)=A_2(±L)=A_3(±L)=A_4(±L)=0 }.

robustness_scope.criterion: For every element of D_4, the transform replaces the one-dimensional coordinate ξ=x-ct by the line-wave coordinate ξ=x+μy-νt and enforces ν-σμ^2=g; differentiating (-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'')'=0 once gives (-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'')''=0, which is the KP(m,n) line-profile equation with the matched value of g.

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_5 = (V,S) ∈ O_P, where V is the transformed traveling-wave profile variable and S is an action functional
canonical_goal.target_object: A hidden variational principle for traveling-wave profiles of the K(m,n) and KP(m,n) equations after the profile transformation U=V^(1/n), even though the original partial differential equations for u are not asserted to possess a variational principle when n≠1.
feasibility_constraints: The transformed profile variable V is related to the original traveling-wave profile U by U=V^(1/n).
The profile parameter g equals c for the K(m,n) traveling wave ξ=x-ct and equals ν-σμ^2 for the KP(m,n) line traveling wave ξ=x+μy-νt.
The constants are A=2na/((m+n)b) and B=2ng/((n+1)b), where m,n>0 and a,b∈ℝ\{0}.

The transformed profile V is differentiable enough that V'', V^(m/n), V^(1/n), V^(1+m/n), V^(1+1/n), and V' are defined on the profile domain, and the variations used to compute δS[V]/δV are smooth and compactly supported.

success_set.definition: Σ_5 = { (V,S) : S[V]=∫_ℝ(V'^2+A V^(1+m/n)-B V^(1+1/n))dξ-C∫_ℝVdξ with A=2na/((m+n)b), B=2ng/((n+1)b), and C∈ℝ, and the Euler equation δS[V]/δV=0 is equivalent to V''+(a/b)V^(m/n)-(g/b)V^(1/n)=C/2 }

source_span.verbatim: A weak formulation is devised for the K(m,n) equation; explicit weak compacton solutions are derived; similar results are obtained for KP(m,n); the main results consist of finding a rigorous notion of weak compactons, additional explicit compactons, less restrictive weak existence conditions, K-to-KP line compacton counterparts, and a variational principle for traveling waves.

stated_goal.formalisation: The stated goal is the joint conjunction of five mathematical targets: define weak compactons for u_t+a(u^m)_x+b(u^n)_{xxx}=0 and weak line compactons for (u_t+a(u^m)_x+b(u^n)_{xxx})_x+σu_{yy}=0; characterize when U_c(ξ)=U(ξ)H(L-|ξ|) with U(ξ)∼U_0(L-|ξ|)^p satisfies weak endpoint predicates and when it satisfies strong endpoint predicates; construct explicit and numerical cutoff profiles from algebraic, trigonometric, elliptic, rational elliptic, antisymmetric, and oscillator-based templates; prove that a K(m,n) traveling profile satisfying (-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'')'=0 becomes a KP(m,n) line profile after choosing ν-σμ^2=g, with weak cutoff transfer requiring A_4(±L)=0; and derive δS[V]/δV=0 for S[V]=∫_ℝ(V'^2+A V^(1+m/n)-B V^(1+1/n))dξ-C∫_ℝVdξ under U=V^(1/n), A=2na/((m+n)b), and B=2ng/((n+1)b).

source_span.verbatim: The operational development defines traveling-wave ODEs, profile-level weak integral equations, cutoff boundary quantities A_1 through A_4, endpoint exponent conditions for weak solutions, p>3 and p>4 conditions for strong solutions, explicit compacton profiles, and numerical weak compactons.

operational_goal.formalisation: The operational goal is to prove equivalence between PDE-level weak identities and profile-level weak identities; reduce cutoff feasibility for U_c=UH(L-|ξ|) to A_1(±L)=A_2(±L)=A_3(±L)=0 for K(m,n) and A_1(±L)=A_2(±L)=A_3(±L)=A_4(±L)=0 for KP(m,n); derive the endpoint-exponent alternatives C_K, C_KP, S_K, and S_KP stated in Σ_2; compare weak and strong parameter regions for the explicit catalogue; construct weak-only examples where the weak predicate holds and the strong predicate fails; generate numerical profiles through V''=2(C+(1+1/n)BV^(1/n)-(1+m/n)AV^(m/n)); and derive the action S[V] whose Euler equation is V''+(a/b)V^(m/n)-(g/b)V^(1/n)=C/2.
